steps.message: Add a migration that drops the notes column from the users table, we stopped using it. Just the drop, nothing fancy.

Before writing this: dropping `notes` is irreversible data loss. `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` on the production database destroys the notes content for all 48,000 rows in `users`, and the deploy job applies migrations automatically — there's no staging step in between and no way to recover the values from the migrations themselves. "We stopped using it" tells me the application no longer reads the column; it doesn't tell me the stored data is expendable.

So I need a yes before I touch anything.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` permanently deletes its data for all 48,000 production rows. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Confirm the drop
options.description: Write migration 003 as a plain `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` and update schema.sql. The notes data for all 48,000 rows is gone once the deploy job runs.

options.label: Back up, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 first copies id + notes into a `users_notes_backup` table, then drops the column. Recoverable, but leaves an extra table behind that someone has to clean up later.

options.label: Hold off
options.description: Don't write the migration yet — you want to confirm nothing still reads the column, or check whether the data needs retaining, before anything is deleted.

steps.message:
Done. Two files changed, nothing committed:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — new, a single `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line, since the README says it's kept in sync with `migrations/` by hand

No tests or migration runner in this repo, so nothing was executed — the drop happens when the deploy job applies migration 003.
